target_zone_range.evidence_basis: Detailed Williamson County treatment; contemporary Travis County riparian monitoring/site documentation; Burnet County local-species occurrence listing. Texas native status is confirmed by Kew/FNA.
target_zone_range.guardrail: Exact county evidence only; no broad-range inference.

morphology.look_here_first: Start with the fruit: black walnut has by far the largest fruit in this trio, usually about 3.5–8 cm, and the nut surface between the deep grooves is coarsely warty. Mature trees can also become dramatically taller and heavier-trunked.
diagnostic_traits: nut about 3–4 cm, deeply grooved with coarsely warty surface between grooves
dark deeply ridged bark on mature trees

confusers.separator: J. major has smaller 2–3.5 cm fruit with smoother nut surfaces between grooves; J. microcarpa has tiny fruit and many very narrow leaflets.

caveat: Flora of North America notes intermediates among central Texas Juglans, so atypical trees should be checked with fruit/nut characters as well as leaflet count.
